groups.title: Personal hygiene and looking after your body

items.bad_habit: Using deodorant to extend the working life of dirty clothes
items.better_action: wash yourself and wear clean clothes.

items.bad_habit: Brushing your teeth only when someone important might smell them
items.better_action: make dental care an everyday routine.

items.bad_habit: Leaving the wet towel in a floor heap, then complaining it smells
items.better_action: hang it to dry and wash it regularly.

items.bad_habit: Leaving beard trimmings, hair or makeup residue as a bathroom signature
items.better_action: clean up after yourself.

items.bad_habit: Emptying the toilet roll without appointing a successor
items.better_action: replace it before leaving.

items.bad_habit: Treating handwashing as an optional finishing touch
items.better_action: wash at the relevant times, including before preparing food.

items.bad_habit: Sharing personal care items because ownership seems complicated
items.better_action: keep personal items separate and care for them properly.

items.bad_habit: Wearing yesterday’s sweaty sports gear because it has dried
items.better_action: wash it and prepare clean gear.

items.bad_habit: Ignoring a persistent health concern because mentioning it would make it official
items.better_action: seek suitable professional advice.

items.bad_habit: Mocking someone for taking care of themselves
items.better_action: support the habit and consider what you could learn.

sources.label: Healthdirect: dental care and teeth cleaning

items.bad_habit: Shopping for the organised person you imagine becoming
items.better_action: plan meals you can realistically prepare and enjoy.

items.bad_habit: Buying a fourth sauce bottle because checking the cupboard takes effort
items.better_action: check supplies before shopping.

items.bad_habit: Starting dinner before discovering what the recipe requires
items.better_action: read the method and organise the ingredients and equipment.

items.bad_habit: Keeping a fridge full of unidentified historic events
items.better_action: label stored food and follow storage and use instructions.

items.bad_habit: Treating a sniff as a complete food-safety assessment
items.better_action: use proper storage guidance and date information.

items.bad_habit: Eating straight from a shared container, then returning it for everyone
items.better_action: serve your portion using clean utensils.

items.bad_habit: Returning empty packets to the cupboard
items.better_action: dispose of them and update the shopping list.

items.bad_habit: Calling a bench full of cooking mess “the chef’s privilege”
items.better_action: include cleaning in the cooking job.

items.bad_habit: Buying takeaway because the groceries require too much imagination
items.better_action: keep a few achievable meals in your repertoire.

items.bad_habit: Criticising every meal while contributing only appetite
items.better_action: help plan, prepare, serve or clean up.

sources.label: Queensland Health: recognising potentially unsafe food

items.bad_habit: Building a rubbish sculpture above the bin
items.better_action: empty it before the contents develop architecture.

items.bad_habit: Putting rubbish beside the bin to save opening the lid
items.better_action: put it in the appropriate bin.

items.bad_habit: Leaving dishes “to soak” until somebody else takes over
items.better_action: wash, dry and put away your share.

items.bad_habit: Vacuuming around the same piles every week
items.better_action: put things away so the floor can be cleaned.

items.bad_habit: Giving every room the same treatment with one filthy cloth
items.better_action: use suitable cleaning equipment and keep it clean.

items.bad_habit: Cleaning only the section visitors can see
items.better_action: agree what the job includes and finish it.

items.bad_habit: Moving clutter from one room into another
items.better_action: decide where it belongs, whether it is needed and who owns it.

items.bad_habit: Leaving spills for the household’s mysterious cleaning spirit
items.better_action: deal with them appropriately and promptly.

items.bad_habit: Keeping broken cleaning equipment because buying it counted as effort
items.better_action: maintain or replace it.

items.bad_habit: Treating a shared toilet as somebody else’s problem
items.better_action: leave it clean and supplied for the next person.

items.bad_habit: Promoting a chair to permanent clothes storage
items.better_action: sort washing from clothes ready to put away.

items.bad_habit: Leaving laundry in the machine until the next person excavates it
items.better_action: finish washing, drying and putting away.

items.bad_habit: Keeping clean and dirty clothes in one democratic heap
items.better_action: give them separate, usable places.

items.bad_habit: Starting every departure with a search for keys, glasses and phone
items.better_action: give essentials a consistent home.

items.bad_habit: Buying storage containers instead of deciding what to keep
items.better_action: sort possessions before buying more storage.

items.bad_habit: Bringing home another “easy restoration” while six projects block the garage
items.better_action: assess the work, space and actual use first.

items.bad_habit: Keeping broken things indefinitely because they might become useful
items.better_action: repair, pass on or dispose of them deliberately.

items.bad_habit: Putting something somewhere “safe” that changes every time
items.better_action: use a place you can remember and retrieve it from.

items.bad_habit: Using the last shared supply and developing selective blindness
items.better_action: refill it, replace it or tell the household.

items.bad_habit: Keeping everyone’s belongings mixed together, then blaming them for losing things
items.better_action: agree accessible places and respect them.

groups.title: Time, attention and getting things finished

items.bad_habit: Snoozing every reminder until it becomes background music
items.better_action: act on it or deliberately reschedule it.

items.bad_habit: Saving an appointment screenshot and expecting destiny to remind you
items.better_action: put the commitment in a usable calendar.

items.bad_habit: Planning an arrival time without allowing for getting ready or travelling
items.better_action: plan the whole departure.

items.bad_habit: Saying yes to commitments that cannot all fit
items.better_action: give an honest answer before others depend on it.

items.bad_habit: Starting another project whenever the current one becomes unglamorous
items.better_action: finish, pause or retire projects deliberately.

items.bad_habit: Watching tutorials instead of practising
items.better_action: use suitable instruction and actually try the skill.

items.bad_habit: Rewriting the to-do list as a substitute for doing it
items.better_action: choose a real task and work through it.

items.bad_habit: Checking every notification while complaining about interruptions
items.better_action: choose when to check messages.

items.bad_habit: Calling something “nearly finished” while everyone waits for the usable result
items.better_action: agree what finished means.

items.bad_habit: Treating asking for help as proof of incompetence
items.better_action: ask a useful question and learn the part you do not know.

items.bad_habit: Buying something because it is discounted rather than wanted
items.better_action: check the need, total cost and budget.

items.bad_habit: Avoiding the bank balance so the money can enjoy its privacy
items.better_action: review spending and upcoming commitments.

items.bad_habit: Collecting subscriptions you no longer remember joining
items.better_action: review recurring charges and cancel unused services.

items.bad_habit: Treating several instalment purchases as several tiny prices
items.better_action: consider all repayments together.

items.bad_habit: Buying duplicates because finding the original seems harder
items.better_action: check what you own first.

items.bad_habit: Borrowing on terms that become conveniently vague
items.better_action: agree the terms and keep your promise.

items.bad_habit: Lending money you need for your own commitments to avoid an awkward conversation
items.better_action: set an honest boundary.

items.bad_habit: Hiding purchases from someone who shares the financial consequences
items.better_action: discuss the shared budget and decisions.

items.bad_habit: Keeping receipts in six vehicles and three washing machines
items.better_action: keep purchase records somewhere retrievable.

items.bad_habit: Spending to look successful while neglecting things you actually value
items.better_action: decide what you want your money to make possible.

sources.label: ASIC MoneySmart: buy now pay later services

items.bad_habit: Treating bedtime as the beginning of tomorrow’s scrolling
items.better_action: make room for a workable wind-down and sleep routine.

items.bad_habit: Giving everyone nearby front-row access to your late-night videos
items.better_action: use headphones and respect their rest.

items.bad_habit: Buying exercise equipment for a person who never arrives
items.better_action: choose movement you can realistically enjoy and return to.

items.bad_habit: Collecting workout videos while remaining seated through all of them
items.better_action: choose an appropriate activity and participate.

items.bad_habit: Turning every friendly game into a personal selection trial
items.better_action: agree the spirit of the game and include everyone’s enjoyment.

items.bad_habit: Copying someone else’s training without understanding it
items.better_action: get suitable guidance for your ability and circumstances.

items.bad_habit: Treating pain or exhaustion as a competition
items.better_action: pause and seek appropriate advice.

items.bad_habit: Scheduling every spare moment until leisure becomes another shift
items.better_action: protect time for rest and unstructured enjoyment.

items.bad_habit: Making every social gathering depend on drinking
items.better_action: include enjoyable options that do not depend on alcohol.

items.bad_habit: Abandoning an activity because you were not immediately impressive
items.better_action: practise with support and notice what improves.

items.bad_habit: Preparing your next story while somebody else speaks
items.better_action: listen and ask a relevant follow-up.

items.bad_habit: Turning every conversation into a comparison you must win
items.better_action: let another person’s experience stand on its own.

items.bad_habit: Giving instructions when a friend wanted someone to listen
items.better_action: ask what kind of support would help.

items.bad_habit: Delivering an apology with a fully loaded “but”
items.better_action: name your action, acknowledge its effect and make amends.

items.bad_habit: Saving unrelated complaints for the next argument
items.better_action: discuss one specific issue at a suitable time.

items.bad_habit: Sending the furious message while your thumbs are still at full throttle
items.better_action: pause and rewrite the actual concern or request.

items.bad_habit: Treating a changed opinion as a public defeat
items.better_action: acknowledge new information and update your view.

items.bad_habit: Using “I’m just honest” to excuse unnecessary cruelty
items.better_action: be truthful with care and a useful purpose.

items.bad_habit: Taking a bad day out on everyone within reach
items.better_action: explain that you are struggling and ask for space or help.

items.bad_habit: Continuing the joke after its target stops laughing
items.better_action: stop, listen and repair the interaction.

items.bad_habit: Treating a date as an audition for your autobiography
items.better_action: show curiosity and make room for their story.

items.bad_habit: Negotiating a declined invitation like a used-car purchase
items.better_action: accept the answer without pressure.

items.bad_habit: Assuming affection gives permission for whatever comes next
items.better_action: check that the other person wants the same thing.

items.bad_habit: Expecting a partner to read clues instead of hearing a request
items.better_action: say what you need clearly and respectfully.

items.bad_habit: Calling jealousy proof of love
items.better_action: discuss boundaries without monitoring or controlling the other person.

items.bad_habit: Keeping a secret scoreboard of every favour
items.better_action: talk about whether the arrangement feels fair.

items.bad_habit: Announcing “I would have helped if you’d asked” after watching the job happen
items.better_action: agree responsibilities and own your share.

items.bad_habit: Leaving one person to organise every enjoyable occasion
items.better_action: contribute ideas, preparation and follow-through.

items.bad_habit: Making jokes about your partner’s private vulnerabilities in public
items.better_action: protect their dignity and keep private matters private.

items.bad_habit: Expecting romance to survive on whatever attention is left over
items.better_action: agree time to enjoy each other’s company.

groups.title: Parenting and the example adults set

items.bad_habit: Shouting “stop shouting” from the opposite end of the house
items.better_action: move closer and model the voice you want.

items.bad_habit: Demanding apologies while refusing to give them
items.better_action: demonstrate acknowledging mistakes and repairing harm.

items.bad_habit: Calling every question backchat
items.better_action: hear the question before deciding how to respond.

items.bad_habit: Doing every manageable task for a child, then calling them incapable
items.better_action: demonstrate, practise together and hand over responsibility.

items.bad_habit: Expecting children to know household skills nobody taught them
items.better_action: show the steps and allow supported practice.

items.bad_habit: Promising family time while remaining absorbed in your phone
items.better_action: protect a period of available attention.

items.bad_habit: Comparing siblings as a motivational strategy
items.better_action: recognise individual effort, needs and progress.

items.bad_habit: Telling children to respect others while mocking strangers yourself
items.better_action: model the behaviour in ordinary situations.

items.bad_habit: Making a child responsible for keeping the adults emotionally settled
items.better_action: seek adult support and let the child be a child.

items.bad_habit: Passing down “that’s how I was raised” without examining the result
items.better_action: keep what helps and learn another way where needed.

groups.title: High-school life, friendships and growing independence

items.bad_habit: Copying an answer to conceal not understanding
items.better_action: ask for an explanation and practise the difficult part.

items.bad_habit: Saving assignment reminders without opening the assignment
items.better_action: read the task and clarify what it requires.

items.bad_habit: Packing yesterday’s bag for today’s timetable
items.better_action: check what the coming day needs.

items.bad_habit: Leaving lunch containers sealed until they become biology projects
items.better_action: unpack, wash and prepare them for reuse.

items.bad_habit: Laughing along with a pile-on to avoid standing out
items.better_action: stop contributing and support the person being targeted.

items.bad_habit: Calling harm “only a joke”
items.better_action: acknowledge the effect and help put things right.

items.bad_habit: Accepting a dangerous dare to protect your reputation
items.better_action: use a refusal you can say and leave with support.

items.bad_habit: Treating somebody’s possessions or family circumstances as their rank
items.better_action: judge how people treat others.

items.bad_habit: Repeating an adult’s hostile behaviour because it looks powerful
items.better_action: practise a response that protects your dignity and other people’s.

items.bad_habit: Assuming one failed attempt proves you are useless
items.better_action: get feedback and try again with appropriate help.

items.bad_habit: Posting the group photo because you look excellent
items.better_action: check whether the other people are comfortable with sharing it.

items.bad_habit: Forwarding screenshots before remembering they contain someone else’s business
items.better_action: check permission and protect private information.

items.bad_habit: Sharing a headline without opening the story
items.better_action: check the source and what the evidence actually says.

items.bad_habit: Leaving incorrect information online because correcting yourself feels embarrassing
items.better_action: make the correction clearly.

items.bad_habit: Giving your phone the best seat at every meal
items.better_action: agree when to put it aside.

items.bad_habit: Staying in an online argument until everyone else falls asleep
items.better_action: ask whether anything useful remains and step away.

items.bad_habit: Calling abuse “gaming banter”
items.better_action: keep competition enjoyable without targeting people.

items.bad_habit: Sharing passwords as proof of friendship or affection
items.better_action: keep accounts secure and respect each other’s privacy.

items.bad_habit: Buying game extras without checking the real-money total
items.better_action: understand the cost and agree spending limits.

items.bad_habit: Recording the entire outing while barely joining it
items.better_action: take some agreed photos, then participate.

sources.label: eSafety Commissioner: sharing photos and personal information

items.bad_habit: Signing task paperwork as though autographing a fan’s shirt
items.better_action: read it, check it fits the job and ask about uncertainty.

items.bad_habit: Treating a new starter’s question as an interruption
items.better_action: explain, demonstrate appropriately and check understanding.

items.bad_habit: Hiding damaged equipment so the next person gets the surprise
items.better_action: report it and follow the workplace process.

items.bad_habit: Reporting hazards into a bottomless suggestion box
items.better_action: acknowledge reports, act and tell the crew what happened.

items.bad_habit: Blaming attitude when the job lacks time, equipment or clear instructions
items.better_action: fix the conditions needed to do the work properly.

items.bad_habit: Calling gear in a walkway “temporary” for three months
items.better_action: provide suitable storage and keep access clear.

items.bad_habit: Returning a borrowed tool without its accessories
items.better_action: check and return the complete kit as agreed.

items.bad_habit: Declaring the job finished while leaving the mess as somebody else’s inheritance
items.better_action: include clearing, storage and handover.

items.bad_habit: Pretending to understand an unfamiliar task to avoid looking new
items.better_action: ask before proceeding.

items.bad_habit: Making speed the only achievement anyone notices
items.better_action: recognise careful work, useful reporting and helping others learn.

groups.title: FIFO camps, travel and the outdoors

items.bad_habit: Conducting a full-volume conversation outside sleeping quarters
items.better_action: move the conversation away from people resting.

items.bad_habit: Treating camp laundry machines as personal storage lockers
items.better_action: collect your washing promptly.

items.bad_habit: Assuming off-shift means available for your entertainment
items.better_action: ask whether someone has time and accept their answer.

items.bad_habit: Packing for six imaginary holidays while forgetting this trip’s essentials
items.better_action: prepare for the actual plans and conditions.

items.bad_habit: Treating the fuel gauge as a test of optimism
items.better_action: plan suitable stops before departure.

items.bad_habit: Assuming phone reception follows you into the scrub
items.better_action: check the trip’s communication and navigation arrangements.

items.bad_habit: Changing a remote-trip plan while your contact follows the old one
items.better_action: communicate relevant changes.

items.bad_habit: Leaving a property gate however it happens to land
items.better_action: follow the property’s instructions and check it is secure.

items.bad_habit: Bringing a dog and announcing that everybody loves dogs
items.better_action: check access rules, care arrangements and other people’s comfort.

items.bad_habit: Leaving rubbish beside a full bin as an act of faith
items.better_action: use suitable disposal or carry it out.

groups.title: Friends, neighbours, clubs and enjoying life together

items.bad_habit: Complaining that the club is dying while the same three people run it
items.better_action: take on a useful job you can reliably complete.

items.bad_habit: Volunteering everyone else for the working bee
items.better_action: ask them and commit your own contribution.

items.bad_habit: Arriving at the shared picnic with a chair and an appetite
items.better_action: agree what to bring or how to help.

items.bad_habit: Saying “probably” to an invitation while waiting for a better offer
items.better_action: give an honest answer and update the host.

items.bad_habit: Returning borrowed gear with a mystery fault and no explanation
items.better_action: report what happened and help resolve it.

items.bad_habit: Greeting newcomers with a test of whether they belong
items.better_action: introduce yourself and explain how to join in.

items.bad_habit: Treating shared venues as places with invisible cleaning staff
items.better_action: leave them ready for the next group.

items.bad_habit: Coaching children from the sideline as though national selectors are listening
items.better_action: encourage effort and let them play.

items.bad_habit: Offering a running commentary while others do the work
items.better_action: ask what help is useful and take part.

items.bad_habit: Waiting for somebody else to organise all the fun
items.better_action: invite people into something achievable and share the preparation.

groups.title: Gardening

items.bad_habit: Buying plants because they look good beside the nursery checkout
items.better_action: choose plants suited to your space, conditions and care capacity.

items.bad_habit: Putting a sun-loving plant wherever the spare pot happens to fit
items.better_action: check the plant’s light and space needs before choosing its home.

items.bad_habit: Planting for the weather you would prefer to have
items.better_action: use suitable local seasonal guidance and the conditions you actually have.

items.bad_habit: Watering everything on autopilot, including yesterday’s puddle
items.better_action: check the plants, soil and weather and follow local water guidance.

items.bad_habit: Giving a struggling plant extra fertiliser before finding out what is wrong
items.better_action: check its growing conditions and seek suitable advice before adding products.

items.bad_habit: Treating fertiliser directions as a conservative opening bid
items.better_action: use products only as labelled and store them appropriately.

items.bad_habit: Leaving tools in the garden until the mower discovers them
items.better_action: clean, check and store tools after use.

items.bad_habit: Keeping a hose across the path because the garden is nearly finished
items.better_action: put it away so people can use the path.

items.bad_habit: Buying seeds for a market garden while owning two usable pots
items.better_action: plan a growing space you can maintain and enjoy.

items.bad_habit: Forgetting what you planted, then asking every green shoot for identification
items.better_action: label plants and keep useful growing notes.

items.bad_habit: Letting weeds set up headquarters while waiting for a heroic cleanup day
items.better_action: identify them and use a suitable local control approach before they spread.

items.bad_habit: Throwing everything into the compost and expecting gardening magic
items.better_action: follow suitable compost guidance and keep unsuitable material out.

items.bad_habit: Planting first and checking the mature size when it reaches the gutter
items.better_action: allow for the plant’s eventual size and nearby structures.

items.bad_habit: Digging as though underground services are somebody else’s plot twist
items.better_action: check the location and requirements for services before ground disturbance.

items.bad_habit: Choosing unfamiliar plants without considering children or pets
items.better_action: check suitability with reliable local guidance before bringing them home.

items.bad_habit: Using a spray because the bottle has a picture of something green
items.better_action: identify the problem and follow the correct product label and conditions.

items.bad_habit: Pruning somebody else’s garden according to your personal artistic vision
items.better_action: ask the owner and learn the suitable method before cutting.

items.bad_habit: Planting edibles without checking the growing site or materials
items.better_action: check that the site, containers and materials are suitable for food growing.

items.bad_habit: Taking the community garden’s harvest while missing every working bee
items.better_action: agree how produce and work are shared and contribute accordingly.

items.bad_habit: Turning gardening into a competition over whose lawn fears them most
items.better_action: choose a useful, manageable garden and make time to enjoy it.

sources.label: Before You Dig Australia: plan before ground disturbance

groups.intro: Grow a garden that fits the place, the people and the time you have. The joke can turn an impulse purchase or a neglected corner into a space somebody actually enjoys.

groups.title: Prepping and emergency preparedness

items.bad_habit: Buying a dramatic survival gadget before learning the local hazards
items.better_action: check official local advice and prepare for the emergencies relevant to your area.

items.bad_habit: Keeping the household emergency plan entirely inside one person’s head
items.better_action: make a shared plan that everyone can understand and access.

items.bad_habit: Treating last year’s emergency kit as a sealed time capsule
items.better_action: check the contents, condition and dates and replace what is needed.

items.bad_habit: Buying supplies for an imaginary siege while everyday essentials run out
items.better_action: use an official household kit checklist and plan around actual needs.

items.bad_habit: Keeping the torch in one drawer and its batteries in a mystery location
items.better_action: store suitable working lighting and its power supply where they can be found.

items.bad_habit: Saving important phone numbers only on the phone that may be unavailable
items.better_action: keep accessible backup contact details as part of the household plan.

items.bad_habit: Waiting for a rumour in the group chat to become the warning system
items.better_action: know the official warning channels for your location and follow current advice.

items.bad_habit: Assuming everybody will find each other without discussing it
items.better_action: agree contact arrangements and meeting options suited to the household.

items.bad_habit: Making a plan that only works for the fastest person in the house
items.better_action: include mobility, communication, medical and other support needs.

items.bad_habit: Remembering the pets when the car is already packed
items.better_action: include animals, their care needs and transport arrangements in the plan.

items.bad_habit: Storing emergency supplies behind furniture nobody can move
items.better_action: keep them secure, accessible and known to the people who may need them.

items.bad_habit: Relying on a single charged device as the entire communications department
items.better_action: plan suitable backup power and ways to receive official information.

items.bad_habit: Packing food that nobody in the household can eat
items.better_action: include suitable dietary needs and items the household can actually use.

items.bad_habit: Buying emergency food once and rediscovering it a decade later
items.better_action: check dates and rotate supplies through ordinary use as appropriate.

items.bad_habit: Leaving essential documents scattered across the house
items.better_action: keep suitable protected copies accessible as part of the plan.

items.bad_habit: Assuming a neighbour will organise your transport without being asked
items.better_action: discuss support and transport arrangements before they are needed.

items.bad_habit: Planning to improvise unfamiliar equipment during an outage
items.better_action: learn its correct use beforehand and follow the manufacturer’s safety instructions.

items.bad_habit: Keeping old contacts and last year’s household arrangements in the emergency plan
items.better_action: review it when people, contact details, needs or living arrangements change.

items.bad_habit: Putting on a brave face while having no idea what the warning means
items.better_action: ask, learn the local warning system and follow the relevant official instructions.

items.bad_habit: Treating being prepared as a reason to distrust everybody nearby
items.better_action: build practical neighbour connections and discuss how to help each other.

sources.label: Get Ready Queensland: make a plan
Get Ready Queensland: pack a kit
Get Ready Queensland: pets and animals

groups.intro: Prepare for the hazards relevant to where you live. A shared household plan, useful supplies and neighbour connections can make being ready part of ordinary life. Use current official guidance for your location and household needs.
